/-!
# The ℙ¹ base case for adelic Riemann–Roch (node `N11a`) and the finite-map gate

This file is part of the **adelic Riemann–Roch lane** (see the lane design document).
It supplies the *base case* of the genus-finiteness keystone and the *gate class*
recording the classical existence of a finite map to the projective line; it does
**not** prove the keystone itself.

## The concrete ℙ¹ cohomology vanishing (`N11a`)

For the standard two-chart cover `{U₀, U₁}` of the projective line `ℙ¹_k`, with
affine coordinate `x` on `U₀` and `x⁻¹` on `U₁`, the Čech `H¹` is the cokernel
```
Γ(U₀ ∩ U₁, 𝒪) / (Γ(U₀, 𝒪) + Γ(U₁, 𝒪))  =  k[x, x⁻¹] / (k[x] + k[x⁻¹]).
```
This cokernel is **zero**, because every Laurent polynomial splits as a
nonnegative-degree part (in `k[x]`) plus a negative-degree part (in `k[x⁻¹]`).
This is `H¹(ℙ¹, 𝒪_{ℙ¹}) = 0`, the base case the keystone reduces to.

We phrase the split purely algebraically, at the level of `LaurentPolynomial R`
submodules, so the keystone can consume it after identifying the ℙ¹ chart rings:

* `Adelic.nonnegLaurentSubmodule R` — `k[x] ⊆ k[x, x⁻¹]`, spanned by `{xⁿ : 0 ≤ n}`;
* `Adelic.nonposLaurentSubmodule R` — `k[x⁻¹] ⊆ k[x, x⁻¹]`, spanned by `{xⁿ : n ≤ 0}`;
* `Adelic.nonneg_sup_nonpos_eq_top` — **the Laurent split**: their sum is everything;
* `Adelic.subsingleton_laurentCokernel` — hence the cokernel is a subsingleton.

## The finite-map gate (node `N9`)

* `Adelic.HasFiniteMapToP1 C` — a single-field `Prop` class asserting the existence
  of a finite `k`-morphism `C ⟶ ℙ¹_k`. This is a **gate** in the `HasPicScheme`
  style: it records a *Kleiman-independent classical existence statement* (any
  nonconstant rational function `x ∈ k(C)` with `[k(C) : k(x)] < ∞` yields such a
  map). It carries **no instance**; the future keystone `N11` consumes it, and the
  proved instance (transcendence degree one of `k(C)/k`) is later work.

## Finiteness of chart preimages under a finite morphism (node `N10`)

* `Adelic.isAffineOpen_preimage_of_isFinite`,
  `Adelic.module_finite_app_of_isFinite` — for **any** finite morphism `π : X ⟶ Y`
  and affine open `V ⊆ Y`, the preimage `π⁻¹V` is affine and its coordinate ring
  `Γ(X, π⁻¹V)` is a *finite module* over `Γ(Y, V)`. The keystone applies these to
  the two standard affine charts of `ℙ¹`, so that with a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` the
  chart preimages `π⁻¹U₀, π⁻¹U₁` are affine with coordinate rings finite over the
  ℙ¹ chart rings `k[x], k[x⁻¹]` (integral-closure finiteness).
-/

/-! ## What separates the order-cone from a degree threshold

The adelic lane's `Adelic.exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` concludes vanishing for every
divisor of **weighted degree** `≥ b`, from a base vanishing, a peel datum and the closed
ledger.  On this carrier the peel and the ledger are both theorems, so it is worth recording
exactly what the remaining distance is — and it is *not* bookkeeping.

`Adelic.coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel` proves, on the adelic carrier, that base-plus-peel
is *equivalent* to vanishing on the whole order-cone `{D' ≥ D₀}`.  There, therefore, the peel
hypothesis is as strong as the conclusion it feeds; here the peel is free
(`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le`), which is the genuine asymmetry between the two carriers.

What no amount of peeling supplies is the step from the **order**-cone to a **degree**
half-space.  `exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing` below isolates that step as a single named
hypothesis, so that a future session sees precisely one obligation rather than a vague gap:
one needs, for each large-degree `D`, *some* divisor `D₀` with `H¹(𝒪(D₀)) = 0` and `D₀ ≤ D`.
That is a cofinality statement about where vanishing occurs in the divisor order, and nothing
in AJC or AJCR currently produces it — for the reason recorded in item 1 of the module
docstring: `deg` is a sum of residue-weighted coefficients, so a divisor can have huge degree
while being small at every point of `supp D₀`. -/

section DegreeThreshold

/-- **From cofinal vanishing to a degree threshold.**  If above every degree bound the
vanishing locus is *cofinal in the divisor order* — i.e. every `D` of degree `≥ b` dominates
some `D₀` at which `H¹` vanishes — then `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0` for every such `D`, and Riemann–Roch
is an equality there.

The hypothesis is exactly the missing input and is deliberately left named and open: this is
*not* a proof of single-field bounded vanishing, it is a reduction of it to one cofinality
statement.  Compare `Adelic.exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod`, which needs a base, a peel and
the ledger; here the peel and the ledger are discharged and only this remains. -/
theorem exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing {b : ℤ}
    (hcof : ∀ D : X.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
      ∃ D₀ : X.CurveDivisor, D₀ ≤ D ∧
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D₀) 1)) :
    ∀ D : X.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) =
        Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
  intro D hD
  obtain ⟨D₀, hle, hvan⟩ := hcof D hD
  exact h0_divisorSheaf_of_subsingleton_of_le K hle hvan

omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
/-- The vanishing half of `exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing`, with no finiteness. -/
theorem subsingleton_of_cofinal_vanishing {b : ℤ}
    (hcof : ∀ D : X.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
      ∃ D₀ : X.CurveDivisor, D₀ ≤ D ∧
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D₀) 1)) :
    ∀ D : X.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
  intro D hD
  obtain ⟨D₀, hle, hvan⟩ := hcof D hD
  exact subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le K hle hvan

end DegreeThreshold

8	/-!
9	# Section drop and the `H¹` peel, on the dévissage sequence
10	
11	Cluster P asks for the *section-drop* results and for `H¹` vanishing.  This file supplies the
12	drop layer and the exact statement of the peel, both **unconditionally** on the χ-ledger's own
13	carrier: the only hypotheses are the five curve binders `ChiLedger.lean` already runs on
14	(`Field K`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `IsIntegral`, `QuasiCompact`, and the two
15	`Module.Finite` cohomology instances, which `ChiCurve`/`Finiteness` discharge at a curve).
16	
17	Everything comes off the six-term slice of the dévissage sequence
18	`0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky_x J → 0` (`Ledger/ChiSlice.lean`), whose third term has
19	`H¹ = 0` because it is a skyscraper.  Two slots of that slice are the whole content:
20	
21	* `H⁰(𝒪(D − x)) ↪ H⁰(𝒪(D))` — `injective_map_f_zero`;
22	* `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))` — `surjective_map_f _ 1`, available because `H¹(sky) = 0`.
23	
24	## What is proved
25	
26	* `h0_divisorSheaf_le_of_le`, `h1_divisorSheaf_le_of_le` — monotonicity of `h⁰` and
27	  antitonicity of `h¹` along a *single dévissage step*.
28	* `h0_sub_point_le`, `h0_le_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg` — the **two-sided section drop**
29	  `h⁰(𝒪(D − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D − x)) + [κ(x) : K]`.
30	* `h0_sub_h0_sub_point_add_h1_sub_h1_sub_point` — the drop **identity**: the `h⁰` gain and
31	  the `h¹` loss add up to the residue degree exactly.
32	* `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_subsingleton_sub_point` (★ the peel) — `H¹` vanishing
33	  **propagates upward** across a dévissage step: if `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) = 0` then `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0`.
34	  This is the one implication the adelic lane can only take as a hypothesis
35	  (`Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`'s peel datum); here it is a theorem of the slice.
36	* `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le` (★) — the same statement along **any** divisor increase
37	  `D₀ ≤ D`, by dévissage induction: `H¹` vanishing is **upward closed on the effective cone
38	  above `D₀`**.  Together with `chi_divisorSheaf` this turns one vanishing into the exact
39	  Riemann–Roch equality `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D` at every `D ≥ D₀`
40	  (`h0_divisorSheaf_of_subsingleton_of_le`), and makes the section drop *exact*
41	  (`h0_eq_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg_of_subsingleton`).
42	
43	**The peel chain uses no finiteness at all.**  Eleven of the nineteen declarations below `omit` both
44	`Module.Finite` cohomology instances: surjectivity of a map is not a dimension count.  That
45	is also why the peel is stated on `Subsingleton (H¹ …)` rather than on `h¹ … = 0` — the
46	latter is vacuously true for an infinite-dimensional `H¹`, since `Module.finrank` reads `0`
47	there, so the `Subsingleton` form is both the stronger statement and the honest one.  The
48	`h¹`-spellings (`h1_le_h1_sub_point`, `h1_eq_zero_of_h1_sub_point_eq_zero`) do need the
49	finiteness, and they carry it.
50	
51	## What this does NOT supply — the three cluster-P items, kept apart
52	
53	Read this before quoting anything above as "uniform vanishing":
54	
55	1. **Single-field bounded vanishing** — "there is `N` such that `deg D ≥ N` implies
56	   `h¹(𝒪(D)) = 0`".  NOT proved here and not implied by anything here.  The peel moves
57	   vanishing *up the divisor order* `D₀ ≤ D`, and a divisor of large *degree* need not
58	   dominate `D₀`; the two are different partial data.  (The adelic lane states exactly this
59	   gap as `Adelic.coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel`; the present file discharges its *peel*
60	   half on this carrier, not its base half.)  A base vanishing `H¹(𝒪(D₀)) = 0` at even one
61	   `D₀` is an input nothing in this file produces.
62	2. **Extension-uniformity** — a bound uniform over finite extensions `K'/K`.  Untouched:
63	   no statement here quantifies over a second field, and `CurveDivisor`/`residueDeg` are
64	   pinned to the single base field `K`.
65	3. **Global generation** — that `𝒪(D)` is generated by its global sections.  Untouched: the
66	   evaluation map at a point does not appear in this file.  `h0_sub_h0_sub_point_lt` is a
67	   *dimension* statement about the drop, not a surjectivity statement about evaluation; the
68	   two agree only when the drop equals the full residue degree, which is precisely what
69	   `Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean` needs and does not get from here.
70	
71	So the honest summary: the **peel** is now unconditional at a curve, and the **base** is not.
72	-/

93

100	
101	variable {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor)
102	
103	omit [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
104	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
105	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in

107	private theorem moduleFinite_devissage_X₃_zero
108	    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] :
109	    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 0) :=

118	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
119	  skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)

121	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
122	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
123	/-- **`H⁰(𝒪(D − x)) ↪ H⁰(𝒪(D))`**: a section with a smaller pole bound at `x` is a section.
124	The left end of the dévissage slice. -/
125	theorem injective_hModule_zero_divisorSheafLE :
126	    Function.Injective
127	      (Sheaf.HModule.map (devissageSES K hx D).f 0) :=
128	  Sheaf.HModule.injective_map_f_zero (devissageSES_shortExact K hx D)
129

131	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
132	/-- **`H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))`** (★ the peel, as a map): the dévissage map is surjective on
133	`H¹` because the skyscraper quotient has no `H¹`.  This is the datum that the adelic lane
134	takes as a hypothesis (`Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`); on this carrier it is a theorem. -/
135	theorem surjective_hModule_one_divisorSheafLE :
136	    Function.Surjective
137	      (Sheaf.HModule.map (devissageSES K hx D).f 1) :=
138	  haveI := subsingleton_devissage_X₃_one K hx D
139	  Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f (devissageSES_shortExact K hx D) 1
140	
141	end Slice

143	/-! ## Monotonicity of `h⁰` and antitonicity of `h¹` across one step -/
144	
145	section Step
146	
147	variable {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor)
148	
149	/-- **`h⁰` grows along a dévissage step**: `h⁰(𝒪(D − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))`, from injectivity at
150	the left end of the slice. -/
151	theorem h0_sub_point_le :
152	    Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) ≤
153	      Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) := by
154	  have hinj := injective_hModule_zero_divisorSheafLE K hx D
155	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 0) :=
156	    inferInstanceAs (Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 0))
157	  exact LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective (f := Sheaf.HModule.map
158	    (devissageSES K hx D).f 0) hinj
159	
160	/-- **`h¹` drops along a dévissage step**: `h¹(𝒪(D)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(D − x))`, from surjectivity of
161	the peel map. -/
162	theorem h1_le_h1_sub_point :
163	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D) ≤
164	      Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
165	  have hsurj := surjective_hModule_one_divisorSheafLE K hx D
166	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) :=
167	    inferInstanceAs (Module.Finite K
168	      (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1))
169	  exact LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_surjective (f := Sheaf.HModule.map
170	    (devissageSES K hx D).f 1) hsurj
171	
172	/-- **The section drop is at most the residue degree**:
173	`h⁰(𝒪(D)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D − x)) + [κ(x) : K]`.  Read off the χ-ledger step together with
174	`h¹(𝒪(D)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(D − x))`: the Euler characteristic gains exactly `[κ(x) : K]`, and the
175	`h¹` term can only help. -/
176	theorem h0_le_h0_sub_point_add_residueDeg :
177	    Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) ≤
178	      Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + X.residueDeg K x := by
179	  have hstep := chi_step K hx D
180	  have hmono := h1_le_h1_sub_point K hx D
181	  rw [Sheaf.chi, Sheaf.chi] at hstep
182	  omega
183	
184	/-- **The drop identity**: the `h⁰` gain plus the `h¹` loss is exactly the residue degree,
185	`(h⁰(𝒪(D)) − h⁰(𝒪(D − x))) + (h¹(𝒪(D − x)) − h¹(𝒪(D))) = [κ(x) : K]`.  This is `chi_step`
186	rearranged, stated in ℤ so that both differences are honest. -/
187	theorem h0_sub_h0_sub_point_add_h1_sub_h1_sub_point :
188	    ((Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) -
189	        Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1))) +
190	      ((Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) -
191	        Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D)) = X.residueDeg K x := by
192	  have hstep := chi_step K hx D
193	  rw [Sheaf.chi, Sheaf.chi] at hstep
194	  omega
195	
196	end Step

198	/-! ## The peel: `H¹` vanishing propagates upward -/
199	
200	section Peel
201	
202	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
203	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
204	/-- **The peel** (★): `H¹` vanishing propagates *up* one dévissage step.  If
205	`H¹(𝒪(D − x)) = 0` then `H¹(𝒪(D)) = 0`, because `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))`.
206	
207	This is the exact statement the adelic lane carries as an unproved peel-surjectivity datum.
208	It is **not** single-field bounded vanishing: it moves a vanishing along the divisor order,
209	and produces no vanishing of its own. -/
210	theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_of_subsingleton_sub_point {x : X}
211	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor)
212	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1)) :
213	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
214	  have hsurj := surjective_hModule_one_divisorSheafLE K hx D

216	  exact ⟨fun a b => by
217	    obtain ⟨a', rfl⟩ := hsurj a
218	    obtain ⟨b', rfl⟩ := hsurj b
219	    rw [Subsingleton.elim a' b']⟩

221	/-- **`h¹` version of the peel**: `h¹(𝒪(D − x)) = 0` forces `h¹(𝒪(D)) = 0`. -/
222	theorem h1_eq_zero_of_h1_sub_point_eq_zero {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)

224	    (h : Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) = 0) :
225	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D) = 0 := by

231	/-! ## Upward closure of `H¹` vanishing on the cone above a divisor
232	
233	The single-step peel iterates.  The induction is `CurveDivisor.induction_devissage` applied
234	to the *difference* `D - D₀`, whose effectivity is what "above `D₀`" means; the predicate is
235	"vanishing at `D₀ + E` for the effective part of `E`". -/
236	
237	section Cone
238	
239	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
240	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
241	/-- **Additive form of the peel**: `H¹(𝒪(B)) = 0` forces `H¹(𝒪(B + x)) = 0`. -/
242	theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_add_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)

244	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K B) 1)) :

248	  have heq : B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 = B := by abel

253	/-- **Peeling a multiple of a point**: `H¹(𝒪(A)) = 0` forces `H¹(𝒪(A + n·x)) = 0`. -/
254	theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_add_nsmul_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)
255	    (A : X.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
256	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
257	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by

259	  | zero => rwa [zero_nsmul, add_zero]
260	  | succ n ih =>

262	      (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ih
263	    have heq : A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 + CurveDivisor.single hx 1
264	        = A + (n + 1) • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 := by
265	      rw [succ_nsmul]; abel
266	    rwa [heq] at hstep
267	
268	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
269	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
270	/-- **Effective peeling**: `H¹(𝒪(A)) = 0` forces `H¹(𝒪(A + E)) = 0` for every effective `E`.

272	`h1_add_effective_le` skeleton of the sibling project's `RiemannRoch/SectionBound.lean`,

274	theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_add_effective (A E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E)
275	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
276	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) := by

279	  intro n

281	  | zero =>

283	    have hE0 : E = 0 := Finsupp.support_eq_empty.mp (Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hc)
